section: Satellite Symposium: Complement and the Brain [1st Sep 2026]
text:
Satellite Symposium: Complement and the Brain [1st Sep 2026]
We are delighted to host a satellite symposium on ‘Complement and the Brain’, running in parallel with the Teaching Day (on Tuesday 1st September 2026). This symposium will focus on the emerging roles of complement in neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative diseases, with presentations ranging from fundamental mechanisms to therapeutic developments.
In the late afternoon of the satellite symposium the keynote will be delivered by Professor Siddharthan Chandran (Director, UK Dementia Research Institute), whose bench-to-bedside work has transformed our understanding of neurodegeneration.
We are grateful to the UK DRI for supporting this event.
Registration is open to all (including those not attending the main conference).

title: Accommodation
text:
Cardiff offers a wide range of hotels from budget to 4-star available in the city centre, all within 10-15min walking distance of the main conference venue (CSL).
You can book your stay directly from the relevant websites. We recommend booking early as hotel rooms can become scarce and more expensive in the summer/autumn months with many major concerts and events happening in the city.
Cardiff University offers some budget-friendly accommodation within our student residences. Please follow this link to check availability, book and pay online for your stay: https://bookaccommodation.cardiff.ac.uk/EMCHD26.bnb

title: Travel
text:
Cardiff is easy to reach from across Europe and beyond. Whether you’re flying in from the US, mainland Europe, or further afield, here’s how to plan your journey:



Direct flights to Cardiff (CWL) via Amsterdam and Dublin.
Alternatively, fly into London Heathrow (LHR), Bristol (BRS), or Birmingham (BHX) – each with easy rail links to Cardiff.





Fly to London Heathrow (LHR) or to Cardiff via Amsterdam or Dublin.
From Heathrow, take the Heathrow Express to London Paddington Station, then a direct train to Cardiff or the Elizabeth Line to Reading and train from there (each ~2.5 hours total).
ternative London airports:
Gatwick (LGW): Gatwick Express to Victoria Station → Tube to Paddington → train to Cardiff.
London City (LCY): DLR and Tube to Paddington.
Stansted (STN) and Luton (LTN): Rail to central London, then Paddington → Cardiff.

All major airports are also served by National Express and Megabus coaches to Cardiff.




Excellent connections via Doha, Dubai, or Istanbul into London or Birmingham.
Continue to Cardiff by train.






From 2025, visitors from the EU, US, Canada, Australia and others will need a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA). Current fee: £16 per person. Apply online here: https://www.gov.uk/eta




Your passport must be valid for the full duration of your stay in the UK.
No visa is required for short visits from many countries – check UK entry requirements.




EU Entry/Exit System (EES)
If travelling onwards to Europe after EMCHD2026, be aware of new biometric checks and longer border times for non-EU nationals.
More on EES here: https://www.government.nl/topics/holidays-and-travels/ees

Our conference venue and social events are all located in the city centre, making it easy to get around on foot. Cardiff is well-connected by train and bus to all major UK cities. title: ECR Events
text:
Early-career researchers (ECRs) are a key component of the European complement network, and we are keen to welcome you all to capital of Wales for EMCHD26. Organised in collaboration between the local organising committee and Early-Career Complementologists (ECCO) we have a selection of great activities to help foster relationships between ECRs and make sure ECRs are at the forefront of the meeting.

ECCO chaired lunchtime discussion session for ECRs – Date TBA
An opportunity for ECRs to discuss their experiences working in the field and provide feedback to the ECN in an anonymous and relaxed environment.







ECR social/Pub quiz hosted at Tiny Rebel – Date TBA
A fun quiz (non-science-based) hosted by ECCO in a popular bar run by the Welsh craft brewery Tiny Rebel located in the centre of Cardiff (CF10 1DD). Limited spaces are available (60) so please indicate during registration that you wish to attend. Food, drinks and prizes will be included!







5th annual ECCO PhD journal article award and talk – Conference session
5th annual ECCO PhD Journal Article Award, sponsored by the European Complement Network (ECN), offering a prize of €500. Applications for this award will be opening soon, and the winner will be announced and be invited to deliver an oral presentation during the ECMHD meeting.


Morning social run club in Bute Park – 7 am, 1st-5th September
The conference is fortunate to have the stunning Bute Park on its doorstep and is perfect for a chatty morning run. Departing every morning from outside the Hilton hotel (CF10 3HH) at 7am and taking in a ~5 km loop of the park it will be a fantastic opportunity for ECRs to network in an informal environment whilst taking in one of the many stunning green spaces Cardiff has.





If you need more information, queries or suggestions for additional activities/events, don’t hesitate to email emchd2026@cardiff.ac.uk. We look forward to welcoming you to Cardiff for an engaging and productive EMCHD meeting.
